meta.title: Labels on the Shelf
meta.textType: functional: product labels read aloud and matched

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, Mom comes home from the shop. She has a large bag with many things in it. Lily puts the things on the shelf, and Tom helps her. "Each thing has a label," says Lily. "We should read it first." The bathroom shelf has a blue bottle of shampoo. The label on the bottle says "SHAMPOO." Next to it, there is a bar of soap in a dish. The label on the dish says, "SOAP. Keep dry." A wet bar of soap goes soft, so Lily keeps it dry.

Tom picks up the shampoo and smells it. "It smells like apples," he says. "Is this juice?" Lily laughs and points at the small words on the label. She reads, "SHAMPOO. Do not drink." "You should not drink it, Tom," she says. Tom smiles and puts the bottle back on the shelf. "I should read the label first," he says. "Now I will read every label."

Then Lily and Tom go to the kitchen. Tom puts a carton of milk on the kitchen shelf. Lily reads the label, "MILK. Keep in the fridge." "Milk should go in the fridge," she says, and she moves it. The shelf also has a bag of flour and a glass bottle of juice. Mom puts the flour in a metal box. "The medicine from the chemist goes on the high shelf," she says. Lily has one more bar of soap for the kitchen. It falls on the floor, and Pip smells it. "Achoo!" sneezes Pip.

Now Mom plays a guessing game. "It is long and soft, and you use it for your hair," she says. "What is it?" "A brush!" says Lily, and Tom finds it in the bag. "Here is one more," says Mom. "It is small and flat, and it has many teeth." "A comb!" says Tom. Lily puts the brush and the comb on the bathroom shelf. Now every thing has a place. "Labels help us, Mom," says Tom.
text.summary: Mom comes home from the shop, and Lily and Tom put the things on the shelves. They read each label, and Mom plays a guessing game.
